theme: God’s love persists; the promise of return
readingInstruction: Read Hosea 12:1-14:9. Hosea ends with a review of Jacob’s story, a final warning, and one of the most beautiful calls to repentance in the Bible. Read chapter 14 slowly, and ask what God promises.
settingTheScene: The last section of Hosea draws on Israel’s history, going back to their ancestor Jacob, and shows how the nation has repeated his deceit. It then moves to a final accusation and the announcement of judgment. But the book does not end in judgment. In chapter 14 God offers words to say, a promise of healing, and a vision of flourishing. It is among the great gospel passages of the Old Testament.
observation: “In the womb he took his brother by the heel, and in his manhood he strove with God” (12:3).
“So you, by the help of your God, return, hold fast to love and justice, and wait continually for your God” (12:6).
“I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; you know no God but me, and besides me there is no savior” (13:4).
“I shall ransom them from the power of Sheol; I shall redeem them from Death. O Death, where are your plagues? O Sheol, where is your sting?” (13:14).
“Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled because of your iniquity” (14:1).
“Take with you words and return to the LORD; say to him, Take away all iniquity; accept what is good” (14:2).
“I will heal their apostasy; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned from them” (14:4).
“I will be like the dew to Israel; he shall blossom like the lily; he shall take root like the trees of Lebanon” (14:5).
interpretation:
Hosea revisits the story of Jacob, the schemer who grasped his brother’s heel and wrestled with God. Jacob is a mirror for Israel: a deceiver, a striver. But Jacob also “wept and sought his favor” and met God at Bethel. The point is that the same God who found Jacob can find Israel. “So you, by the help of your God, return.” Repentance is possible, with God’s help.

Chapter 13 contains a reminder that God alone is the Savior. “You know no God but me, and besides me there is no savior.” This is a central claim of the Bible. And in the middle of the chapter, there is an astonishing promise: “I shall ransom them from the power of Sheol; I shall redeem them from Death.” Paul quotes this in 1 Corinthians 15:55, as a proclamation of the resurrection. Even in a chapter about judgment, God declares that he will defeat death.

Chapter 14 is the climax. It begins with a call: “Return, O Israel.” Then God gives them words to use. “Take with you words.” Repentance should not be left to chance. God provides the language: take away all iniquity, accept what is good, we will no more say to the work of our hands, “Our God.” Israel is to confess, to turn from false hopes, to trust in God alone. “In you the orphan finds mercy.”

God’s reply is stunning. “I will heal their apostasy; I will love them freely.” The word “freely” means without any cost, without conditions. This is grace. God’s anger has turned away. The language of the garden follows: dew, lily, roots, branches like an olive tree, fragrance like Lebanon, grain, vine. It is a picture of life and fruitfulness. The barren, unfaithful nation will flourish. “From me comes your fruit.”

The book ends with a wisdom question: “Whoever is wise, let him understand these things.” The ways of the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble. The hearer must choose.
connection: Paul quotes Hosea 13:14 in 1 Corinthians 15:55: “O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?” Christ’s resurrection fulfills it. Romans 3:24 says we are “justified by his grace as a gift,” echoing “I will love them freely.” Jesus said, “I am the vine; you are the branches… apart from me you can do nothing” (John 15:5). Hebrews 13:15 calls us to offer a sacrifice of praise, “the fruit of lips that acknowledge his name,” echoing Hosea 14:2.
application:
Use Hosea 14:2 as a prayer of repentance today. Say the words God provides.

Receive the promise: “I will love them freely.” What would change if you believed it?

Ask where you are trusting in Assyria, horses, or the work of your hands rather than in the LORD.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to take away all iniquity and accept what is good in you.
Tell him you return to him, and heal your apostasy.
Ask him to be like the dew to you.
